post.description:
Public: this is how a person gets a session. Creates the account and, in the same transaction, its membership of the workspace - creating the workspace first if the install has none. On success it sets the session cookie exactly as login does.

Single-workspace model: when a workspace already exists the new account joins it as a member. There is no invitation or approval step yet (ADR 0004), so until there is, anyone who can reach this endpoint can join - do not expose it beyond a trusted network.

A duplicate email answers 409 `email_taken`. That reveals the address is registered, which a registration endpoint cannot avoid; it costs the same time as a success.

Session only: a token caller gets 403 `insufficient_scope`, so a leaked token cannot mint more. The response carries the credential in `token`; it is returned this once and only a hash is kept.

A token may do only what its `scopes` name. An unknown scope is 422 `unknown_scope` and nothing is created.

post.description: One write per drop: sets `status_id` and `position` together. Send at most one of `position`, `before_id` and `after_id` (more is a 422); none puts the ticket at the end of the column. `before_id`/`after_id` name a live ticket in the target column, or the answer is a 422 `neighbour_not_found` at that member. Written like any edit: version + 1, announced as `ticket.updated`, and `If-Match` makes it conditional. When there is no room between two neighbours the target column's other tickets are renumbered; each of those is written like an edit (version + 1) and announced as `ticket.updated`, before the moved ticket's own event.

Omit it for a plain last-write-wins write.
